title: The Harbor of the Cape Route
premise: In 1974, as the colonial republic collapses, Ulyana Almeida — a courier who has spent two decades carrying coded ledgers and learning which silences keep people alive — returns to the harbor town of her youth just as the army requisitions it and seizes the ledger bearing every name she once protected. Racing the victors' historians, who will write the record first, she must recover the ledger's missing pages, confront the officer who once loved her and now serves the new order, and decide whether truth or mercy matters more. In the end she testifies before a commission neither side controls, trading her own safety for the names on record, and chooses exile over silence — but not alone.
about_author: Ivo Oyelaran is the pen name of a former archivist who spent years cataloguing declassified diplomatic correspondence from collapsed states. The Harbor of the Cape Route is their second novel, drawn from fragments of testimony found misfiled in a naval customs house.

chapters.title: Salt on the Manifest
chapters.summary: Ulyana arrives in the harbor town aboard a coastal freighter under a false manifest, twenty years after fleeing it. POV: Ulyana. She surveys the docks that remember her better than its people do. Emotional beat: wary homecoming, the ache of returning to a place that was never allowed to be home.

chapters.title: The Requisition Order
chapters.summary: The army seals the town; soldiers post requisition notices naming the customs house and its ledgers. Ulyana watches from a boarding-house window as crates of records are hauled out. POV: Ulyana. Beat: dread crystallizing into purpose — the ledger with the names is in those crates.

chapters.title: Which Silences Keep People Safe
chapters.summary: Flashback to 1954: young Ulyana learns courier craft from her mentor Tomás, memorizing codes and, more importantly, when to say nothing. POV: Ulyana (past). Beat: tenderness shadowed by foreboding; we learn why silence became her native language.

chapters.title: The Man Who Counts Crates
chapters.summary: Captain Duarte Ferreira, now overseeing the records seizure, recognizes Ulyana at the checkpoint — and lets her pass without a word. POV: Duarte. He remembers the woman he loved before duty split them. Beat: suppressed longing tangled with suspicion; he is not sure whose side history will say he was on.

chapters.title: Ledger of Names
chapters.summary: Ulyana infiltrates the customs house at night and finds the ledger shelved for transport — but the final pages, the ones with the protected names, have been cut out. POV: Ulyana. Beat: cold panic; someone got there first, and only three people could have known where they were hidden.

chapters.title: The Historian's Advance Party
chapters.summary: A victors' historical commission arrives to 'curate' the record, led by the polished Dr. Salgado, who interviews townsfolk and rewrites as he listens. POV: Salgado. Beat: chilling banality; history as logistics, and Ulyana realizes her deadline is his itinerary.

chapters.title: Aunt Beatriz Remembers Differently
chapters.summary: Ulyana visits her aunt, a fishmonger whose memory of the 1954 disappearances contradicts the official version — and who has kept one torn ledger page sewn into a market apron for decades. POV: Beatriz. Beat: fierce, stubborn love; the first page recovered, at a price.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Tea
chapters.summary: Duarte summons Ulyana for questioning that is really an oblique conversation between old lovers, each probing what the other knows about the missing pages. POV: alternating close third. Beat: love against duty made literal over a teapot; both leave having lied.

chapters.title: The Second Courier
chapters.summary: Ulyana discovers a living legend: Rui, believed executed in 1955, alive as the commission's local fixer — the man who cut out the pages to sell them back to the victors as insurance. POV: Rui. Beat: betrayal wearing a familiar face; survival has made him a merchant of memory.

chapters.title: What Tomás Never Burned
chapters.summary: Searching her dead mentor's boathouse, Ulyana finds his cipher key and a letter revealing the pages were split three ways deliberately — a failsafe so no single betrayal could erase the names. POV: Ulyana. Beat: grief transmuted into resolve; the plan of the dead becomes the map of the living.

chapters.title: Curfew, and a Confession
chapters.summary: Under curfew, Duarte finds Ulyana at the seawall and admits he saw the requisition list weeks ago and did nothing — his complicity laid bare. POV: Duarte. Beat: the cost of obedience confessed; he offers her one favor, knowing it may end him.

chapters.title: The Page in the Chapel Wall
chapters.summary: Following Tomás's cipher, Ulyana retrieves the second cache from behind the chapel altar during a funeral Mass, nearly caught by Salgado's clerks cataloguing parish registers. POV: Ulyana. Beat: sacred tension; the past literally embedded in the town's prayers.

chapters.title: Salgado Makes an Offer
chapters.summary: Dr. Salgado, having identified Ulyana, proposes she 'contribute' her memories to the official history — sanitized, attributed, safe. POV: Salgado then Ulyana. Beat: seduction of legitimacy; she sees exactly how her life would be laundered into their narrative.

chapters.title: Rui's Price
chapters.summary: Ulyana tracks Rui down and bargains for the third set of pages; he demands passage out on her escape route and immunity in whatever record she writes. POV: Rui. Beat: bitter negotiation between two survivors; she pays, despising herself a little for understanding him.

chapters.title: The Night the Harbor Went Dark
chapters.summary: A blackout — sabotage by retreating loyalists — plunges the town into darkness; in the confusion, soldiers begin burning 'surplus' records in the customs yard. POV: ensemble, anchored by Ulyana. Beat: terror and opportunity entwined; the fire that could destroy everything also covers her theft.

chapters.title: Ash and Cipher
chapters.summary: Ulyana rescues armfuls of burning documents while decoding the reunited pages by matchlight: the full list of the disappeared, including names the new regime would prefer never existed. POV: Ulyana. Beat: revelation as burden; the truth is heavier than she imagined and cannot be carried alone.

chapters.title: Duarte's Choice
chapters.summary: Ordered to certify the destruction of the records, Duarte instead falsifies the inventory and passes Ulyana the transport schedule for the commission's archive convoy. POV: Duarte. Beat: duty finally breaking toward love; he knows this act defines him forever, whichever way historians rule.

chapters.title: The Convoy Road
chapters.summary: Ulyana and Beatriz intercept the archive convoy on the cape road, substituting the true ledger for Salgado's curated copy minutes before military police sweep the route. POV: Ulyana. Beat: breathless climax of nerve; the swap succeeds, but Rui sells them out to buy his own exit.

chapters.title: Testimony Before the Commission
chapters.summary: Arrested and brought before Salgado's panel, Ulyana speaks the names aloud into the official transcript, forcing them onto the record no matter how the summary is spun. POV: Ulyana. Beat: the novel's moral summit; silence ends here, at maximum personal cost.

chapters.title: What the Victor Writes
chapters.summary: Salgado, outmaneuvered — the transcript exists, copies already moving through church and press channels — must let the names stand even as he buries Ulyana's role. POV: Salgado. Beat: ambiguous victory; history is compromised but no longer wholly theirs.

chapters.title: Departures
chapters.summary: Released but marked, Ulyana prepares to leave on the last coastal steamer; Duarte, facing inquiry, chooses to stay and answer for his uniform. They part at the quay with everything unsaid finally said. POV: alternating. Beat: love honored by separation rather than betrayed by convenience.

chapters.title: The Harbor Keeps Its Own Record
chapters.summary: Years later, an aging Ulyana reads a smuggled pamphlet printing the names in full, credited to 'the couriers of the Cape Route.' On the harbor shore, she adds one stone to a cairn the town has quietly built. POV: Ulyana. Beat: resolution — memory outlives regimes; the record, like the tide, belongs to everyone now.
